citeAs: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu (2021). Inter-GPS: Interpretable Geometry Problem Solving with Formal Language and Symbolic Reasoning. arXiv:2105.04165.
creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu (UCLA, Zhejiang University, Sun Yat-sen University)
description: Geometry3K is a large-scale benchmark for geometry problem solving consisting of 3,002 multi-choice geometry problems collected from two high-school textbooks (grades 6-12). Each problem includes problem text, a geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and a correct answer, and is densely annotated with formal language descriptions covering diverse geometric shapes and problem goals.
name: Geometry3K
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each problem is annotated with: problem text literals (formal language), diagram literals (formal language), problem goal label, and geometry shape label. For human performance evaluation, each annotator answered 10 problems; multiple annotators evaluated the test split via Amazon Mechanical Turk.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were described as well-trained with undergraduate degrees. No further demographic details (nationality, age, gender) are provided.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (used for human performance evaluation on the test split; annotators required to have high school or higher degree, answer 10 problems in 25 minutes, spend at least 7 minutes on the problem set and 10 seconds per problem)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem and annotated each problem text and diagram with dense formal language descriptions (literals composed of predicates and arguments). Problems were also labeled with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes. The formal language uses 91 predicates organized into six categories: geometric shapes, unary geometric attributes, general geometric attributes, binary geometric relations, A-IsXOf-B-type geometric relations, and numerical attributes and relations.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from two popular online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline) that provide high-school geometry textbooks for students across grades 6-12. Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. Each problem was also labeled with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: SAT-style geometry problems from two high-school textbooks available via two online digital libraries: McGraw-Hill (https://www.mheducation.com/) and Geometryonline (www.geometryonline.com). Each raw problem consists of problem text in natural language, a geometry diagram image, and four multiple-choice candidate answers.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: Less than 1% of problems in Geometry3K can be solved without the associated diagram, making it highly diagram-dependent. The dataset covers only high-school geometry (grades 6-12). The symbolic solver may fail due to inaccurate parsing results and an incomplete theorem set. Diagram parsing tends to fail with ambiguous annotations or multiple primitives. The text parser struggles with nested expressions and uncertain references. The solver cannot handle complex problems with combined shapes and shaded areas.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each problem was annotated with formal language descriptions via: (1) rule-based text parsing using regular expressions to translate problem text into formal literals; (2) diagram parsing using Hough Transformation to extract geometric primitives (points, lines, arcs, circles), RetinaNet for symbol and text region detection, and MathPix OCR for text recognition. Symbol grounding was formulated as an optimization problem with geometric constraints. Problems were split into train/validation/test sets with ratio 0.7:0.1:0.2 (2,101/300/601).
rai:dataSocialImpact: The work may inspire following research in symbolic reasoning and interpretable models and facilitate education. Problems are collected from online open sources.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking geometry problem solving algorithms; training and evaluating automatic problem parsers (text and diagram parsers) that translate problems into formal language; training and evaluating symbolic reasoning solvers; facilitating research in interpretable math problem solving and education.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: RetinaNet (neural object detector used in the diagram parser to extract diagram symbols and text regions); MathPix OCR tool (used to recognize textual content in diagrams); Hough Transformation (used to extract geometry primitives from diagrams); BART (transformer model used as a semantic text parser baseline).
